title: RPISEC MBE: introductory reversing in a VM
license_review: Code is BSD-2-Clause; lecture slides use CC BY-NC 4.0. This plan references code/VM setup only and does not redistribute slides.
check_meaning: Record behavior and an incorrect-input comparison for the introductory binary under the selected lab account. A local account/password or whoami result is learner-controlled evidence; the plan does not claim a trusted exploitation grade.
availability_reason: The original wargame requires a separate VM with matching 32-bit environment. The README warns its system setup script must not run on a personal host. VM artifact checksum, image compatibility and snapshot/teardown measurements are pending.

runtime_acceptance: Reviewed VM archive hash, expanded size and guest architecture
Provider-owned VM/disk inventory and isolated network
Guest reset, host interruption, export and complete disk teardown
Measured cold/warm disk and RAM/CPU use

integration.start: Import a checksum-reviewed original VM into a dedicated Linux VM provider; start lab01 using its documented lab1C account. Never run setup_wargame.sh on the host.
integration.check: Use the guest debugger to compare the expected binary behavior and a deliberately incorrect input; record tool and binary versions.
integration.stop: Use the selected VM provider to power off or suspend the same VM; retain its disk and exported notes for resume.
integration.reset: Export work before discarding the owned environment and restoring its reviewed baseline. No reset is automated until lifecycle acceptance passes.
integration.export: Keep notes and scripts separate from the VM disk. Full disk snapshots stay on the learner PC.
integration.destroy: Remove only the dedicated VM and owned scratch disks after exporting work. Provider-specific VM IDs and a restore-tested baseline are prerequisites to automation.

instructions: Record behavior and an incorrect-input comparison for the introductory binary under the selected lab account. A local account/password or whoami result is learner-controlled evidence; the plan does not claim a trusted exploitation grade. Use lab plan for requirements and the exact report template. Imports are manual practice observations and never enable runtime execution.
